text.p: Post-Communist Foreign direct investment (FDI) into Slovakia totalled $845 million between January 1990 and September 1996, up from $808.4 million for the January 1990-June 1996 period, the Slovak Statistical Bureau said on Friday.
"Against the (end of) the second quarter of this year, the FDI increased by 1.1 billion crowns, $36.6 million, or 4.7 percent," the SUSR said in a statement.

It said investment from neighbouring Austria led all countries, totalling 5.6 billion crowns, followed by Germany with 5.1 billion crowns, the Czech Republic with 3.9 billion crowns, the United States with 2.6 billion crowns and Britain with 1.6 billion crowns.

Some 40.3 percent of all investment went to the industrial sector, with 33.4 percent in the trade sector and 17.2 percent in the financial sector, the SUSR said. -- Peter Laca, Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-563-3687
